description:
FILED s484d (2026-09-14), measured on four companion rows.

`tools/pclperl-for-tests` runs the child's SBCL with `2> $dir/err` and then
SCRUBS that file of implementation noise -- `^;` compiler-note blocks,
`STYLE-WARNING:`, "compilation unit finished" -- before re-emitting it,
precisely because a real perl child prints none of it and the harness
compares the child's output byte for byte (its own comment says so).

The scrub is defeated by a program that redirects its own stderr.  perl's
`run_multiple_progs` writes this preamble into every record program:

    BEGIN { push @INC, '.'; open STDERR, '>&', STDOUT or die ... }

so the child's `*error-output*` IS its stdout from then on, and SBCL's
compile-time diagnostics for the forms that follow go down the stdout pipe,
where the scrubber never looks.  Measured: t/op/anonsub.t record 4 (a sub
defined in a string eval -> "undefined function: main::pl-Y" plus a 12-line
note block), two records of t/op/tie.t and one of t/op/runlevel.t -- 4 rows
that fail ONLY on the noise (the child's actual answer is correct in
anonsub.t's case).

FIX SHAPE, at the source instead of the sink: muffle the conditions rather
than filtering their text, so it does not matter where the stream points.
`tools/pclperl-for-tests` builds one `--eval` form that reads and evals the
program; wrapping that loop in

    (handler-bind ((style-warning #'muffle-warning)
                   (sb-ext:compiler-note #'muffle-warning)) ...)

removes exactly the two classes the scrubber already drops.  Keep the
scrubber (it also catches the `PCL Runtime loaded` line and the loader's
context note), and do NOT widen the muffle to `warning`: a full WARNING can
be about the program, and perl-level warnings are plain text written by
`pl-warn`, not CL conditions, so they cannot be muffled by this.

BAR: it changes what every child prints, so it owes the full sweep (the
sweep's own children go through the same script) and the io/+run/+op/ legs of
the companion.  Cheap discriminating measurement first: `grep -c` the
companion's kept outputs for `^# ; ` and `caught style-warning` to count the
rows that would move.
subject: A child program's SBCL compiler diagnostics reach the COMPARED output once the program redirects STDERR to STDOUT -- pclperl-for-tests' scrubber cannot see them any more
